changes.text: FireRed on Windows and Android, with its sound.
Savestates (F5), fast-forward, fullscreen.
Play together over the network: the Wireless Adapter, the Link window (F2), online codes.
Settings (F4), with keys and controller buttons.
The debug menu (F3).
The Mystery Gift events: the Aurora and Mystic Tickets.
The players of other copies on your map: walking, running, cycling, surfing.
Choose how the others see you (F6).
Export and import the save (debug menu).
Extras: instant text, running indoors and always, skipping the replay, trade evolutions by level.
Resume where you left off when the game starts again.
Emotes over your head (E), names over the players nearby, and the players on the Town Map.
A friend list in the Link window.
Trade and battle with the players nearby, anywhere.
DexNav (F7): the wild Pokémon of each map.
Extras for reusable TMs and move tutors.
Easier on phones: less battery, a steady fast-forward.
The summary shows IVs and EVs (A on its SKILLS page) and the stats a nature raises and lowers.
Pokémon editor (F8): IVs, EVs and natures (an extra).
Mints, bottle caps and EV-lowering berries, on Celadon's 5F (an extra).
The first Pokémon in the party follows you, with HeartGold's sprites (an extra).
HeartGold's Pokémon pictures in battles and menus (an extra).
MOVES in the party menu: remember forgotten moves, forget others.
The touch L and R buttons work in open windows.
NAME in the party menu: a new nickname for a Pokémon, anywhere.
Physical or special by the move, as from Diamond and Pearl: FIRE PUNCH hits with ATTACK.
The Fairy type: Clefairy, Gardevoir, Marill, Mawile... and CHARM, SWEET KISS and MOONLIGHT.
Pokédex data: SELECT on a Pokédex page shows the base stats, abilities, evolutions and every move it learns.
The changelog, in the MENU. On a PC, Esc (or Y on a controller) opens the MENU.
The B that closes a window no longer reaches the game under it.
Real-time battles (an extra): wild Pokémon and trainers fought right on the map, A B L R for the moves.
All 353 moves in real time, a camera that follows the fight and four looks for the bars and buttons.
Dodge with a direction pressed twice. SELECT swaps Pokémon, START opens the battle's menu.
Trainers as hard as you choose (Very hard at first), double battles, and boss fights with the gym leaders, the Elite Four and more.
Wild Pokémon with their own ways of fighting, sometimes two at once. A dazed one is easier to catch.
Combos, a rank after each win, aim help, cover behind trees, and tall grass that catches fire.
The following Pokémon keeps its colors after the quest log's replay.
The Game Corner+ (an extra): Celadon's Game Corner full of new games, each named over its machines.
VOLTORB FLIP from HeartGold and CARD FLIP from Gold and Silver.
MAGIKARP DERBY, WHO'S THAT POKéMON?, POKé PLINKO, STAT SHOWDOWN and a SHELL GAME.
A prize shop of six Pokémon a day, the same for everyone, with their nature, stats and level, rerolled for coins.
The TMs and held items in the shop, one of them a daily deal.
An egg machine: today's eggs by rarity, 1 in 1024 shiny, almost ready to hatch.
The battle type in Settings > Extras: Original or Real-time.
Trainers are fought in an arena of their own: a flash, a clearing in the forest, then back where you were.
Classic clear: a see-through look for real-time battles.
Hordes: your one Pokémon against two or three wild ones.
Your Pokémon runs around you to the front as a battle starts.
A caught Pokémon's ball stays where it landed, with three stars at the click.
Grass no longer catches fire in real-time battles.
The sounds of wind and ice moves playing on after the battle.
Foes off the screen walking through trees and walls.
Touch taps quicker than a frame were sometimes missed; every press counts now.

On the phone, real-time battles get their own touch buttons: a stick that comes where your thumb touches (any angle, slower when pushed a little), the four moves around the right thumb in their types' colors, filling up as they recharge, a DODGE button, and SWAP and START at the top right.
A controller's left stick moves your Pokémon at any angle in real-time battles, slower when pushed a little.
MENU > Touch buttons: drag each touch button wherever you want and set how see-through they are, for the normal and the battle layouts.
Outside battles the touch D-pad is now a cross like the GBA's (between two arms presses both); the round pad stays as an option in MENU > Touch buttons.
The battle stick can come where your thumb lands, as before, or stay fixed at its place: a choice in MENU > Touch buttons.
MENU > Touch buttons: tap a button to select it and make it bigger or smaller (50% to 200%); tap the background to unselect.
The party menu groups a Pokémon's field moves under FIELD (in blue) when it knows more than one, and has POKéDEX to open its Pokédex page.

The touch D-pad gives 4 directions, so a thumb a little off left or right no longer walks the player up or down (8 directions stay as an option in MENU > Touch buttons). A direction holds until the thumb is clearly into the next one, and the thumb is followed past the D-pad's edge.

On Android the touch buttons vibrate: a click for each button pressed, a lighter tick for each new D-pad direction (Android 10 and later). VIBRATION in MENU > Touch buttons sets how strong, from off to 100% in steps of 25.
The cross D-pad is drawn sharper, with a thinner edge and slightly rounded corners, and is bigger and a little closer to the picture by default.
A trainer battle started in a cave is fought in a cave arena (rock walls, blocks of rock and piles of stones to hide behind, craters) instead of the forest.
FLASH lighting a dark cave went off after a trainer battle in the arena; it now stays on.

A new battle type, Classic on map (Settings › Extras › Battle type): the game's own battle by turns, fought right on the map with the real-time battles' looks. Everything works as in a battle: the bag, the party, catching and nicknames, learning moves, double battles aimed at a foe, evolving after.
In Classic on map, a battle's first words, a fainted foe and the EXP gained pop up on the map and go away by themselves (the EXP in blue beside your Pokémon).
Classic clear is the look battles on the map start with.
Fast-forward works in battles of every type; it used to wait during real-time battles.
Settings › Extras › No fast-forward in battles: every battle at the game's speed, whatever its type.
In Classic on map, trainers are fought right where they stand instead of in the arena.
In Classic on map, gym leaders are fought in a stadium of their own: a battle hall with its court, you on the green mark, the leader on the red one, people watching from the sides.
Beating a gym leader in his gym could freeze the game (64-bit and Android) or double the prize money: his long words at the end ran past the battle's text and over its settings.
In Classic on map, a badge's fanfare plays during the leader's words, with its pause, as in a battle.
Classic on map is the battle type at first, and No fast-forward in battles is on at first (a choice already made stays).

After a battle on the map, your Pokémon evolve right there: it glows and changes back and forth between its forms with sparkles (B stops it), then learns its new moves, a fifth one through the summary.
Playing together, the other players' following Pokémon walk behind them on your map too, shiny or not, as they do in their game.
In battles on the map, a wild Pokémon you've already caught has a Poké Ball by its name, and a trainer's Pokémon show as a row of balls, grey once fainted, in every look.
People and item balls at the edge of the view could come back one square off after a battle on the map moved the camera (Silph Co's item balls); they stay on their squares now.
After a win or a buy in the Game Corner+ (a Voltorb Flip round, a Derby race, the shop, the egg machine), the music stayed paused, and walking out of the Game Corner left the screen black for good.
L and R work on the Game Corner+ screens: Voltorb Flip's marks, the prize shop's L/R and reroll, and the egg machine's ten eggs opened the HELP screen out of sight instead.
The Game Corner+ screens' help lines fit on the screen (they were cut off at the bottom, and the shop's at the right).
Voltorb Flip's numbers sit clear of the edges: the line boxes' Voltorb count no longer runs past the box, and the round's coins no longer touch THIS ROUND.

The Game Corner+ games are rebalanced: games of skill pay a good player about what the slots give, games of luck give the bets back on average (Who's That Pokémon 4 coins an answer, Stat Showdown x1.3, the Shell Game's easy rounds x1.25, Plinko and Card Flip fair, the Derby's house 3% and odds up to x50).
The names over the Game Corner's machines sit inside their boxes (they hung a few pixels low).

The girl at the left of the Game Corner's counter buys the Pokémon in your PC for money: box by box, each with her price (stronger, rarer, higher-level, better-IV Pokémon are worth more, and a shiny one is worth 50,000 more than any other); held items go back to the bag.

Hitmontop Roulette in the Game Corner (the right wall's two lower machines): a casino's European roulette with HITMONTOP spinning round the wheel for the ball, every casino bet at its odds, and the last 60 numbers with how often each kind came.
